Being in circumstances that remind me of the event (eg, being in the dark).
avoid anything that could be stressful

Threat.value: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger
I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place

Memory.value: The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me
Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time
When memories come to mind of what happened, I feel my body is in the same position as when the frightening event occurred.

vignette: Mr. Tran was a 72-year-old South Eastern Asian man who had lived in the United States for over four decades. He had immigrated to the country with his wife when he was in his early thirties and had since devoted himself entirely to caring for their home and family. In recent years, Mr. Tran found himself acting as a nanny for his grandchildren while they were young, providing a sense of continuity and stability for his family. The trauma that now haunted him had begun years ago when he was in his early sixties. His wife, whom he adored deeply, had developed a severe drinking problem that escalated into bouts of physical abuse against Mr. Tran. Each incident left him feeling violated and shattered, unable to reconcile the woman he loved with the person who inflicted such pain on him. The most vivid memory for Mr. Tran was one dark evening where his wife attacked him with a wooden spoon while they were in their home alone. He remembered her red-rimmed eyes, the fear and despair that had gripped them both during those moments. Even now, he found it hard to process the trauma as something that happened to him; the memory felt alien, like it belonged to someone else. Each time he recalled the event, a wave of terror engulfed him, and his body tensed up, reenacting the same protective posture from that night. This trauma had led Mr. Tran into a labyrinth of avoidance behaviors. He never allowed himself to feel or express anger, believing that it would only worsen the situation and provoke further violence. Being in circumstances that reminded him of those dark nights was unbearable; he found himself avoiding being alone in dimly lit rooms, feeling as if danger lurked around every corner. Mr. Tran also tried to avoid any stressors that could trigger painful memories or feelings, even going so far as to limit his interactions with others to keep the peace. Mr. Tran’s startle responses had become increasingly severe over time. Simple movements in the environment, such as a sudden rustling sound outside the door, made him jump and react as if he were back in that frightening moment. He found it nearly impossible to relax even when he knew he was safe at home with his wife or grandchildren present. This constant state of hypervigilance had begun to strain his relationships; his wife noticed a change in his demeanor, often asking what was wrong but never receiving a clear answer. As a nanny, Mr. Tran’s job required him to be attentive and nurturing towards the children. However, he found himself increasingly on edge around them, especially if they were playing loudly or suddenly entering a room without warning. He tried to hide these reactions from his family, fearing that they would see him as fragile or incapable of caring for the children properly. The constant tension had taken its toll on Mr. Tran’s health and well-being. He knew he needed help but was hesitant about speaking openly about his trauma, fearing judgment and stigma. What frightened him most was the fear that he might lose control again in a similar situation or that his past would continue to define who he is. Finally, it was his wife who encouraged him to seek professional help, recognizing how much pain he was enduring silently. Mr. Tran’s primary hope now was to regain some semblance of peace and stability in his life. He hoped to learn strategies to manage the intrusive memories and avoidant behaviors that had come to dominate his existence. Through therapy, Mr. Tran sought to find a way to integrate his traumatic experiences without them dictating every aspect of his daily life. His journey was about reclaiming control over his emotions and finding a path towards healing and acceptance.
